key_insight: PerceptionRubrics replaces broad, holistic multimodal scoring with fine-grained atomic audits that better reflect how humans actually judge images and captions. It aims to make evaluation more calibrated, consistent, and resistant to benchmark saturation.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the mismatch between high benchmark scores and poor real-world robustness in multimodal models. Existing evaluations often miss small but important errors because they rely on coarse semantic matching rather than precise human-like judgments.
method: Builds a dataset of 1,038 information-dense images paired with 12,000+ instance-specific rubrics.
Creates golden captions using a Circular Peer-Review consensus pipeline to derive reliable, human-aligned criteria.
Distills the rubrics into a dual-stream evaluation system with Must-Require and Must-Avoid checks for atomic auditing.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more trustworthy way to measure multimodal model quality and catch subtle failures that standard benchmarks overlook. It can improve model selection, debugging, and safer deployment by aligning evaluation with human perception.
